source_text: Quod si eam maximam dici Zeno non siverit, qui tantam virtutum copulam unitatemque confirmat, ut ubi fuerit una, omnes dicat adesse virtutes et, ubi una non fuerit, omnes deesse; atque illam veram esse virtutem, quae hac quadrua iugalitate perficitur; tunc quoque nobis plurimum praebebit auxilii, cum docuerit, nec prudentiam, nec fortitudinem, nec temperantiam posse sine iustitia contineri; secundum quam veritatem et Ecclesiastes pronuntiat: Qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet [n29] .
pass_a_gloss: Which if Zeno will not have allowed it to be called the greatest, who confirms so great a coupling and unity of virtues that where one has been, he says all virtues are present, and where one has not been, all are absent; and that that is true virtue which is perfected by this fourfold yoking; then too he will furnish us very much help, when he has taught that neither prudence nor fortitude nor temperance can be held together without justice; according to which truth Ecclesiastes also pronounces: Who has sinned in one will lose many good things.
pass_b_english: Suppose Zeno does not allow justice to be called the greatest. He maintains such a close connection and unity among the virtues that, where one is present, he says all are present, and where one is absent, all are absent. True virtue, he says, is perfected by this fourfold union. Even then he will give us great help by teaching that wisdom, courage, and self-control cannot exist without justice. Ecclesiastes speaks in accordance with this truth: 'Whoever sins in one thing will lose many good things' (Ecclesiastes 9:18).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: The Ecclesiastes quotation preserves Julian's wording, “sins in one thing”, rather than substituting the wording of a modern translation.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
